newsitem.title: USA: Reply period ends for DOT decision on ValuJet.
newsitem.headline: Reply period ends for DOT decision on ValuJet.

text.p: The objection and reply period to the U.S. Transportation Department's tentative approval for ValuJet Inc. to resume flights ended Monday and the department said it was now weighing a final decision.
Department spokesman William Mosley said there was no deadline for the final decision.

ValuJet was grounded June 17 for repeated violations of federal aviation safety regulations. The tentative approval to allows it to resume operations was issued August 29, after the carrier instituted new safety procedures.

Mosley said there were 18 objections to the tentative decision during the seven day comment period, including one from the Association of Flight Attendants, which argued that the low-cost Atalnta-based carrier remained unsafe.
He said 15 responses to the objections were made during the four-day reply period, including one on Monday by ValuJet,
Mosley said the department would analyze the objections and responses before issuing its final decision.
